name: Gang of Four
label: EMI
lede: Four Leeds students named themselves after a Chinese political purge, walked off Top of the Pops rather than change one word, and made a guitar sound so sharp and funky that Flea, Kurt Cobain and Michael Stipe all admitted to borrowing it.

eras.title: A pun on a purge
eras.text: Gang of Four came together in Leeds in 1976 among university students steeped in Marxist theory, Situationism and dub reggae. Their debut single on a tiny Edinburgh label went to No. 1 on the indie chart, and John Peel did the rest.

years.h: Jon King, Andy Gill and Hugo Burnham start a band in Leeds
years.p: Singer [[Jon King|e2472ddb-f53f-4853-b839-2ed07e2d4064]], guitarist [[Andy Gill|eb3f978d-272a-460d-bc3e-a1a82ecb8147]] and drummer [[Hugo Burnham|9c965e30-7658-4658-b5f2-08fff1874bd2]] start with bassist Dave Wolfson. After two gigs [[Dave Allen|829dc2aa-99d2-44ad-ad1e-76533b14d512]] replaces him.

years.h: The Mekons' Andy Corrigan names them from a headline
years.p: Driving with Andy Gill and Jon King, Andy Corrigan of [[The Mekons|66d2169c-dea5-46d3-b4cb-52ed87b24ab0]] spots a newspaper headline about China's Gang of Four, the purged Maoist faction, and suggests the name.

years.h: Damaged Goods EP on Fast Product
years.p: Edinburgh's Fast Product releases Damaged Goods with (Love Like) Anthrax and Armalite Rifle. It goes to No. 1 on the indie chart, and two [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] sessions follow.

eras.title: Entertainment, and a walkout
eras.text: EMI signed them, and Gang of Four made a debut album that still sets the standard for post-punk: King's lyrics about commodities, work, sex and the Troubles over Gill's jagged, stop-start guitar and a rhythm section that played like a funk band. Then they walked away from the biggest TV show in Britain.

years.h: Gang of Four walk off Top of the Pops over one word
years.p: Booked on the BBC's Top of the Pops for At Home He's a Tourist, the band is told to swap a word about condoms for a cleaner one. They refuse and walk off.
years.xp: The BBC then kept them off its radio and TV, and EMI's enthusiasm cooled. At Home He's a Tourist still reached No. 58, the band's highest UK chart placing.

q: Gang of Four could really swing. I stole a lot from them.
years.h: Entertainment! on EMI, Warner Bros. in America
years.p: Recorded at the Workhouse on London's Old Kent Road and produced by Andy Gill, Jon King and manager Rob Warr. King's cover shows a cowboy and a Native American shaking hands, each fooling the other.
years.xp: Rolling Stone's David Fricke called it the best debut by a British band since the Clash's. [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] put it among his 50 favorite albums, and [[Flea|2dc7a305-7a8c-4fcc-add4-5e9def0a9a0d]] said it completely changed the way he looked at rock music. It had sold over 100,000 copies in the UK by 2009.

eras.title: Bass players, a banned uniform and the end
eras.text: The original four split up one member at a time. Dave Allen left, a Parliament bassist filled in, and Sara Lee brought a smoother, more radio-ready bottom end just as the Falklands War made one of their best songs untouchable. By 1983 it was over.

years.h: Solid Gold, sparse and severe
years.p: Gang of Four's second EMI album picks apart war, work and leisure in songs like Cheeseburger, He'd Send in the Army and In the Ditch.

years.h: Dave Allen leaves to form Shriekback
years.p: Dave Allen quits to start [[Shriekback|748161b8-ec62-4423-b6f1-3a8026190ebb]] with ex-[[XTC|97c86b2c-2765-46a2-aef8-76a7e24c430f]] keyboardist Barry Andrews. Busta 'Cherry' Jones, who'd worked with [[Parliament|d1947987-9614-49ae-bd36-8000e6b6f7d0]] and [[Talking Heads|a94a7155-c79d-4409-9fcf-220cb0e4dc3a]], fills in; then Sara Lee of Robert Fripp's League of Gentlemen joins.

years.h: The BBC bans I Love a Man in a Uniform
years.p: I Love a Man in a Uniform, from Songs of the Free, is pulled from BBC airplay during the 1982 Falklands War, just as it looked like their radio breakthrough.
play: I Love a Man in a Uniform

years.h: Hugo Burnham leaves to form Illustrated Man
years.p: Drummer Hugo Burnham quits. He later drums for PiL and ABC, manages Shriekback, and becomes an A&R man in New York.

years.h: Hard, then the band dissolves
years.p: Jon King, Andy Gill and Sara Lee make one more EMI album, Hard, and Gang of Four breaks up.

eras.title: Gill and King, twice more
eras.text: Andy Gill and Jon King revived the name as a duo with hired hands for two albums on Polydor. The records were modern-sounding and little-loved, but the name kept its pull.

years.h: Mall, with Gail Ann Dorsey on bass
years.p: Andy Gill and Jon King reunite on Polydor for Mall, with [[Gail Ann Dorsey|3363921c-9099-40af-93cc-1b15d0e46fc5]], later David Bowie's bassist.

years.h: Shrinkwrapped, and quiet again
years.p: Gill and King's second Polydor album, Shrinkwrapped, closes the 1990s version of Gang of Four.

eras.title: The original four, and the last split
eras.text: With Franz Ferdinand, Bloc Party and The Rapture all sounding a lot like them, the original line-up reunited for the first time since 1981. It lasted two years; Gill and King lasted until 2012.

years.h: Jon King, Andy Gill, Hugo Burnham and Dave Allen reunite
years.p: The original Gang of Four reunite in November 2004 and tour the UK in January 2005, then the US twice that year.

years.h: Return the Gift: the old songs recut
years.p: Gang of Four re-record songs from Entertainment!, Solid Gold and Songs of the Free, with remixes.

years.h: Hugo Burnham and Dave Allen leave again
years.p: Mark Heaney replaces drummer Hugo Burnham, who was teaching at the New England Institute of Art in Boston. Dave Allen also leaves; by Content the bassist is Thomas McNeice.

years.h: Content, the last album with Jon King
years.p: Produced by Andy Gill at his London studio, Content gets four stars from the New York Times' Jon Pareles, who says the band had reclaimed its old attack.

years.h: Jon King and Andy Gill part; Gill keeps the name
years.p: After the Content tours, King and Gill disagree about direction and stop working together. Gill carries on as Gang of Four with singer John Sterry, against King's wishes.

eras.title: Andy Gill's Gang of Four
eras.text: For eight years Gang of Four was Andy Gill and a younger band, making records with guests from The Kills to German rock star Herbert Grönemeyer. It ended when Gill died at 64, weeks after a tour of China.

years.h: What Happens Next, with Alison Mosshart
years.p: The first Gang of Four album with John Sterry singing features [[Alison Mosshart|054f94f3-2a75-480b-b417-d817cdbcf6f6]], [[Herbert Grönemeyer|456eabce-d1dd-4481-a206-36ab4f2eaeb8]] and guitarist Tomoyasu Hotei. Andy Gill is the only original member left.

years.h: Happy Now, Andy Gill's last album
years.p: Self-released on Gill's own label, Happy Now is the last Gang of Four album Andy Gill completes.

years.h: Andy Gill tours China with Gang of Four
years.p: Andy Gill takes Gang of Four on a tour of China in November 2019.

years.h: Andy Gill dies in London at 64
years.p: Andy Gill dies on February 1, 2020. His death was first put down to pneumonia and multiple organ failure; according to Wikipedia he was later found to be an early victim of COVID-19, after the China tour.
years.xp: Gill had also produced the [[Red Hot Chili Peppers|8bfac288-ccc5-448d-9573-c33ea2aa5c30]]' 1984 debut, [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]]'s Blue, [[Killing Joke|f5aca88c-e3c1-4bc2-af33-68a9a9f7b56a]] and [[The Futureheads|0cf9d983-aecf-4d57-9e94-fde2beac014f]]. His widow is the journalist Catherine Mayer, co-founder of Britain's Women's Equality Party. Two EPs of his last recordings, This Heaven Gives Me Migraine and Anti Hero, came out after his death.

eras.title: The Long Goodbye
eras.text: A tribute album and a box set brought the classic records back, and Jon King and Hugo Burnham brought the band back with them, first with David Pajo of Slint on guitar, then Ted Leo. They called the last tour the Long Goodbye, then kept finding reasons to play.

years.h: The Problem of Leisure: a tribute to Andy Gill
years.p: The Problem of Leisure: A Celebration of Andy Gill and Gang of Four gathers other artists covering the band's songs.

years.h: Jon King, Hugo Burnham, Sara Lee and David Pajo reunite
years.p: Gang of Four return with King, Burnham and Lee from the early 1980s line-up and [[David Pajo|85188c46-d3ed-4517-ba78-5d06ec764f1c]] of [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]] in Andy Gill's place.

years.h: The 77-81 box set earns Jon King a Grammy nod
years.p: The Gang of Four 77-81 box collects the classic era. Jon King's art direction gets a 2022 Grammy nomination, and the band tours the US behind it.

years.h: The Long Goodbye tour, with Ted Leo on guitar
years.p: Gang of Four announce their last headlining tour of the US and Europe: Jon King and Hugo Burnham with [[Ted Leo|3b7051df-c423-4d90-a6ca-aa10c363445d]] on guitar and [[Gail Greenwood|d86b84e3-6c11-4499-a453-82e8744bc08e]] on bass. King's memoir To Hell With Poverty! also comes out in 2025.

years.h: Dave Allen dies at 69
years.p: Original bassist Dave Allen dies at 69. Hugo Burnham told Stereogum that Allen had been living with early-onset dementia for several years.

years.h: Not quite goodbye: Wilco's Solid Sound
years.p: Gang of Four are announced for [[Wilco|9e53f84d-ef44-4c16-9677-5fd4d78cbd7d]]'s Solid Sound Festival at MASS MoCA, explaining that the Long Goodbye was only their last headline tour.

years.h: No Kings Here!, the first song without Andy Gill
years.p: Produced by Nick Launay, who worked on 1981's Another Day/Another Dollar, the single backs the 2026 No Kings protests. It's the first Gang of Four song with Jon King in 15 years.
years.xp: It's also Hugo Burnham's first new Gang of Four recording in about 44 years, the first with Ted Leo and Gail Greenwood, and the first Gang of Four song ever made without Andy Gill.
